<div class="ref-table">

| Attribute and property | What it does |
|---|---|
| `definition` | One of definition or src is required. The property takes the object. Refused (datum-error, nothing replaced) while a src fetch is still loading: clear src first.<br>**Takes** JSON of a form definition. **Default** none. |
| `src` | Fetched on connect; a later change refetches, and a form an earlier src brought is replaced. Refused (datum-error, nothing fetched) while a definition the page assigned is in place: clear definition first. A response longer than max-definition-bytes is refused before it is parsed.<br>**Takes** URL of a definition. **Default** none. |
| `max-definition-bytes`<br>`maxDefinitionBytes` | The longest definition read from src, in UTF-8 bytes, the cap every other import has; a longer one is reported as datum-error and not parsed. Anything but a whole number above 0 is reported and the cap stays.<br>**Takes** whole number of bytes. **Default** 2097152 (2 MiB). |
| `mode` | readonly keeps the answers as sent.<br>**Takes** interactive \| readonly. **Default** interactive. |
| `locale` | The starting locale, negotiated against the form's supported locales; auto takes the visitor's browser languages. Switching later never resets an answer.<br>**Takes** BCP 47 tag \| auto. **Default** the form's default locale. |
| `language-switcher`<br>`languageSwitcher` | Shows the locale switcher in the form's header.<br>**Takes** boolean attribute. **Default** off. |
| `chrome` | Header, footer and other parts a host merges over the definition's own. The language-switcher, frame and frame-fixed attributes still apply beside it, merged in; where both give the same setting (a frame, a language-switcher part), the chrome's wins.<br>**Takes** JSON of the chrome parts. **Default** none. |
| `frame` | A default the author's own pick beats, unless frame-fixed. Short for chrome.frame; with a chrome that names a frame, the chrome's frame is used instead.<br>**Takes** seamless \| outlined \| paper \| a frame the binding defines. **Default** the binding's own. |
| `frame-fixed`<br>`frameFixed` | Makes frame beat the author's pick. Applies to the frame attribute, not to a frame the chrome names.<br>**Takes** boolean attribute. **Default** off. |
| `heading-level`<br>`headingLevel` | The level of the form's top heading; headings the form draws itself sit one level under it.<br>**Takes** 1 to 6. **Default** 1. |
| `debug`<br>attribute only | Logs journey diagnostics to the console.<br>**Takes** boolean attribute. **Default** off. |
| `messages` | Validation message templates by code. An entry wins over the message the definition authors for that code; codes it leaves out keep the definition's words.<br>**Takes** JSON of message overrides. **Default** none. |
| `texts` | The renderer's own strings (buttons, status lines).<br>**Takes** JSON of UI text overrides. **Default** none. |
| `submitting-placement`<br>`submittingPlacement` | Where the Submitting status line shows. Listing both draws a visual echo at the bottom so the line is announced once. Any other word is reported as an error.<br>**Takes** top, bottom, or both separated by spaces or commas. **Default** top. |
| `confirmation` | Present: an accepted submit shows the form's own confirmation, a notice with the reference the delivery's reply carries, if it has one. It never replaces a receipt the page set itself with setNotice. Worded through texts keys confirmationTitle, confirmationMessage and confirmationReference (English built in). Read when a submit is accepted; changing it rebuilds nothing.<br>**Takes** boolean attribute. **Default** off. |
| `error-summary`<br>`errorSummaryPlacement` | Where the error summary shows after an invalid submit; none leaves only the inline messages. Any other word is reported as an error.<br>**Takes** top, bottom, or both separated by spaces or commas; none. **Default** top. |
| `data-sources`<br>`dataSources` | The form paints first while its sources load. The property takes sources with functions.<br>**Takes** JSON of a data source set. **Default** none. |
| `data-source-wait`<br>`dataSourceWait` | all holds the form until every source has answered.<br>**Takes** none \| all. **Default** none. |
| `data-source-timeout`<br>`dataSourceTimeout` | 0 for no limit.<br>**Takes** milliseconds. **Default** 15000. |
| `translations` | The host's translations of the form's texts; an entry overrides the definition's own translation of the same address.<br>**Takes** JSON of a translation catalog: locale, then kind (form, components, chrome, journeys, pdf), then the owner's id, then the property tree, with string leaves. **Default** none. |
| `values` | Seeds the answers; setting later replaces them.<br>**Takes** JSON of initial answers. **Default** none. |
| `host-context`<br>`hostContext` | Facts about the visit the rules read, such as host.role. Plain JSON data only: a function, NaN or a Date is left out and reported as datum-error host-context.invalid. Changing it updates the form in place and keeps the answers typed so far. For display only: it is not sent with a submission, and a server judges host. rules with values of its own.<br>**Takes** JSON object of the values host. names read. **Default** none. |
| `draft` | A key: answers auto-save under it (the browser's storage unless draft-store or the draftStore property says otherwise) and restore on return.<br>**Takes** storage key. **Default** none. |
| `draft-store`<br>`draftStore` | Where the draft key's draft is kept. server:&lt;url> (on the page's origin, or one allow-origins lists; relative URLs read against the page) speaks four requests, &lt;id> being the draft key: PUT &lt;url>/&lt;id> saves the draft as JSON, GET &lt;url>/&lt;id> answers it (404 when there is none), DELETE &lt;url>/&lt;id> removes it (404 counts as removed), GET &lt;url> lists the drafts. local is the browser's storage. Anything else is reported as datum-error. A server on another origin is reported as datum-error and drafts stay in the browser. A draftStore object assigned from script wins; it is the route for headers, credentials, another origin or another protocol. Does nothing without draft, and nothing when features leaves drafts out.<br>**Takes** server:&lt;url> \| local. **Default** local (browser storage). |
| `features` | Present means only the listed features exist; minimal is a single-page form that renders, validates and submits. The attributes and properties of a feature can only narrow a listed feature, never enable one the list omits. What the page or the definition asks of a left-out feature is ignored with one console warning, its methods reject, and its files (the PDF module, the sandbox, the WebAuthn code, the server validator) are never requested. A word with a minus in front takes that feature out: all -drafts is every feature but drafts, and so is -drafts alone, since a list of only exclusions starts from all; an exclusion wins wherever it stands. A word that names nothing (a mistyped exclusion included) is reported as datum-error and left out, and a list holding one never starts from all, so a typo can only narrow. agent is opt-in: not part of all; write all agent to add it (the agent tools a browser assistant can call through WebMCP, and agentTools() / executeAgentTool() for page script, from a lazy chunk). Changing it rebuilds the runtime, and the answers typed so far carry over; an agent-only change only registers or withdraws the agent tools.<br>**Takes** space or comma list of journeys, print, translations, data-sources, drafts, server-validation, signing, pdf, wasm, agent; presets all, minimal; -name leaves one out. **Default** absent: every feature but agent. |
| `agent-access`<br>`agentAccess` | With the agent features token: the host enforces, the definition decides, or the host forbids. always: the host enforces, so the tools are registered whatever the definition says (the author's agentTools: off included). definition, the default: the definition decides, so root.configuration.agentTools allowed is live and off or absent is registered sealed (every call answers agent-off, except describe_form, which says the form is the person's to fill). never: the host forbids, so nothing is registered or loaded for this element. Without the token it does nothing. Changing it never rebuilds the form.<br>**Takes** always \| definition \| never. **Default** absent: definition. |
| `pdf` | auto fetches datum-pdf.js beside the bundle on the first PDF. A loaded module is the pdfSupport property; a template resolver is the pdfTemplates property. Held to the page's origin: a URL on another origin is reported as datum-error and the attribute is treated as absent, unless allow-origins lists that origin; the property may name any.<br>**Takes** auto \| URL of the PDF module. **Default** unset (no PDFs). |
| `pdf-integrity`<br>`pdfIntegrity` | Holds the PDF module pdf names to a hash, as script integrity does: the module is fetched, its bytes checked, and those bytes imported from a blob: URL (list blob: in script-src under a Content Security Policy), on the first load and on every retry. A module that does not match is never run and the PDF fails saying why. integrity.json in the package, beside dist, lists every file's sha384.<br>**Takes** sha256-, sha384- or sha512- digests, space-separated. **Default** unset. |
| `pdf-manifest`<br>`pdfManifest` | Where the package's integrity manifest is; read only with pdf-manifest-integrity. Resolved against the page when set. Not held to the page's origin: the file is held to a hash.<br>**Takes** auto \| URL of integrity.json. **Default** auto: ../integrity.json from the PDF module (the npm package's layout, as the CDNs serve it). |
| `pdf-manifest-integrity`<br>`pdfManifestIntegrity` | Holds integrity.json to a hash, then each font file the PDF module fetches (fonts/) to the hash the manifest lists for it; a font it does not list or whose bytes differ is refused and the PDF fails. A PDF theme's own faces belong to another package and are not checked.<br>**Takes** sha256-, sha384- or sha512- digests, space-separated. **Default** unset (the fonts are fetched unchecked). |
| `pdf-theme`<br>`pdfTheme` | The theme the PDF is drawn with when the render call and the layout name none; it outranks the binding's suggestion.<br>**Takes** PDF theme id (default, or a registered id). **Default** unset: the PDF theme the form's binding suggests, else default. |
| `pdf-unknown-components`<br>`pdfUnknownComponents` | What a PDF does with a component it has no rendition for: ignore draws it generically and says nothing, warn does the same and reports component.unknown, fail rejects the PDF.<br>**Takes** ignore \| warn \| fail. **Default** warn. |
| `formula-errors`<br>`formulaErrors` | What a rule formula that cannot be read does: fail refuses the form, warn drops the rule and says so.<br>**Takes** fail \| warn. **Default** fail. |
| `risky-patterns`<br>`riskyPatterns` | Whether a regular expression that could run away is refused.<br>**Takes** refuse \| allow. **Default** refuse. |
| `wasm` | auto fetches datum-wasm.js beside the bundle and runs the validation sandbox in the page, for development and testing. In production the server validates. A page that imported the module assigns wasmValidationHost; plugins and external data are properties. Held to the page's origin: a URL on another origin is reported as datum-error and the attribute is treated as absent, unless allow-origins lists that origin; the property may name any.<br>**Takes** auto \| URL of the sandbox module. **Default** unset. |
| `wasm-log-level`<br>`wasmLogLevel` | How much the sandbox's run log keeps; the log arrives on datum-wasm-validated.<br>**Takes** off \| error \| warn \| info \| debug. **Default** warn. |
| `wasm-timeout`<br>`wasmTimeout` | How long the page waits for the sandbox module to load; 0 waits without limit. A module that never loads blocks the submit with an error.<br>**Takes** milliseconds. **Default** 15000. |
| `wasm-integrity`<br>`wasmIntegrity` | Holds the sandbox module wasm names to a hash, as script integrity does: the module is fetched, its bytes checked, and those bytes imported from a blob: URL (list blob: in script-src under a Content Security Policy). A module that does not match is never run and the submit reports the sandbox unavailable. integrity.json in the package, beside dist, lists every file's sha384.<br>**Takes** sha256-, sha384- or sha512- digests, space-separated. **Default** unset. |
| `signing-scope`<br>`signingScope` | What a signed submission covers. Providers are the signingProvider(s) and pdfSigner properties (functions); the attribute sets the scope inside the signing property.<br>**Takes** envelope \| submission \| values. **Default** envelope. |
| `signing-placement`<br>`signingPlacement` | Where the signature sits in the delivered submission; the attribute sets the placement inside the signing property.<br>**Takes** embedded \| wrapper. **Default** embedded. |
| `sign-with`<br>`signWith` | The id of the provider every submit signs with; no provider of that id refuses the submit (signing.providerMissing).<br>**Takes** provider id. **Default** none. |
| `change-on`<br>`changeOn` | When a typed value counts as settled for datum-change: input reports after change-debounce ms of quiet or on leaving the field, commit only on leaving the field. Any other word is reported as an error.<br>**Takes** input \| commit. **Default** input. |
| `change-debounce`<br>`changeDebounce` | The quiet time for change-on input; 0 reports every write.<br>**Takes** whole milliseconds. **Default** 300. |
| `journey` | Which journey runs: an id, form for the whole form on one page, or journey for the definition's default journey. Changing it restarts the journey over the answers typed. On a definition that has journeys, form still loads the journeys runtime (the journey can be switched later without a rebuild), so a missing runtime file shows the error card even then.<br>**Takes** journey id \| form \| journey. **Default** the definition decides. |
| `page` | Opens the journey on that page when the person may reach it (a deep link, a resume point); nextPage and previousPage move it, and reading the property gives the page shown.<br>**Takes** page id. **Default** the journey's first page. |
| `validate-url`<br>`validateUrl` | Where a journey's server check posts, as the { document, scope, pageId } delivery a Datum host's POST /api/submissions/validate takes; a serverValidator property wins over it and is the custom validator. Held to the page's origin: a URL on another origin is reported as datum-error and the attribute is treated as absent, unless allow-origins lists that origin; the property may name any.<br>**Takes** URL. **Default** none. |
| `validate-timeout`<br>`validateTimeout` | How long a journey's server check may take before the service counts as unavailable. Read when the form is built: changing it rebuilds the runtime, and the answers typed so far carry over.<br>**Takes** whole milliseconds; 0 for no limit. **Default** 10000. |
| `allow-origins`<br>attribute only | The other origins the wasm, pdf, draft-store and validate-url attributes may name. A word that names no origin (*, a bare host) is reported as datum-error and left out. Changing it applies an attribute it now allows and drops one it no longer does.<br>**Takes** space-separated origins, each written as a URL (https://cdn.example). **Default** none: the page's own origin only. |
